div.head: VI As 12.3

ab.seg: ⁊ se cyng cwæð eac, þæt man nænne ne sloge for læssan yrfe þonne XII pæniḡ weorð, buton he fleon wille oððe hine werian, þæt man ne wándode þonne, þeah hit læsse wære.
Gif we hit þus gehealdað, þonne gelyfe ic to Gode, þæt ure frið bið betera, þonne hit æror wæs.
Et rex etiam iussit (Precepit etiam rex), ne aliquis occidatur pro minori precio quam duodecim denarios ualens, nisi fugiat uel repugnet, ne dubitetur tunc, licet minus sit.
Si hęc ita conseruemus, in (domino) Deo confido (confidimus), quod pax nostra melior erit quam fuit (fuisset) antea.
⁊ se cyng cwæð eac, þæt man nænne ne sloge for læssan yrfe þonne XII pæniḡ weorð, buton he fleon wille oððe hine werian, þæt man ne wándode þonne, þeah hit læsse wære.
Gif we hit þus gehealdað, þonne gelyfe ic to Gode, þæt ure frið bið betera, þonne hit æror wæs.

Und der König verordnete auch, dass man niemanden wegen geringeren Betrages als 12 Pfennig Werth hinrichte, es sei denn, der wolle fliehen oder sich wehren: dass man dann [freilich] nicht Bedenken trage, auch wenn es weniger ist. —
Wenn wir es so beobachten, dann traue ich zu Gott, dass unser Rechtszustand besser sein wird, als er früherhin gewesen ist.

And the king also ordained that no one should be put to death for a smaller amount than 12 pence' worth, unless he will flee or defend himself: that then [indeed] one should not hesitate, even if it is less.
If we observe it thus, then I trust in God that our state of law will be better than it was before.

And the king has further declared, that no one shall be slain for the theft of property worth less than 12 pence unless he is minded to flee or defend himself. But in that case there shall be no hesitation, even if the property is of less value.
If we observe the provisions as stated above, I believe, before God, that the security of our realm will be better than it has been in the past.

And the king said also, that no one was to be killed for a [theft of] property worth less than 12 pence, unless he tried to flee or defend himself; in that case one was not to hesitate, although the amount involved were less. If we maintain it thus, then I trust to God that our peace will be better than it was before.

div.note: Whitelock translates VI As 12.3 as one clause, which the sheet divides into rows 12.3[a], 12.3[b]; her translation of the whole is given here, in the first row.

Dieser Satz bringt inhaltlich nichts Neues, er wiederholt 1, 1 und, z. T. mit denselben Worten, II 1, 2 = VI 12, 1⁷. Das zum Schluss redende Ich kann nur der König sein; die Gilde hat also ein Staatsgesetz nur abgeschrieben. — Vgl. Gl Frieden 1a. e

This sentence adds nothing new in substance; it repeats 1, 1 and, partly in the same words, II 1, 2 = VI 12, 1⁷. The ‘I’ speaking at the end can only be the king; the guild has therefore merely copied a law of the State. — Cf. Gl Frieden 1a. e
Cf. VI As. cap. 1 § 1, II As. cap. 1.
